=== CHARACTER LOCK — STRICT ===

RIVEN:

Use the provided Riven reference image as the strict primary character reference.

Preserve Riven's facial identity, pale-blonde hair, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing and armor design, large sword design, and overall appearance exactly as shown in the reference.

Riven is an experienced soldier.

Her large sword remains exactly consistent with the reference.

At the beginning of this scene, Riven has no reason to believe this mission is personally connected to her.

She listens to the military briefing seriously and professionally.


ALLY SOLDIER:

Use the provided Ally Soldier reference image as the strict primary character reference.

Preserve his facial identity, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing, armor design, weapon design, and overall appearance exactly as shown in the reference.

This is the SAME Ally Soldier from the previous scenes.

He stands near Riven during the briefing.

He listens seriously and behaves naturally as a soldier receiving new orders.


COMMANDER:

Create one male military commander approximately 45–50 years old.

He is a veteran career soldier.

Weathered mature face.

Short dark hair with some natural gray.

Short beard or heavy stubble.

He wears practical dark weathered steel armor with worn leather and restrained faded burgundy military details.

His equipment is slightly better than that of ordinary soldiers but remains practical and battle-worn.

He carries a normal officer's sword.

The Commander is disciplined, calm, authoritative, and emotionally restrained.

He is NOT an obvious villain.

Do not give him sinister expressions.

Do not give him fantasy villain armor.

Do not make him shout unnecessarily.

He treats the mission as a normal military operation.


=== CHARACTER COUNT ===

The THREE important characters are:

1. Riven
2. Ally Soldier
3. Commander

Other ordinary allied soldiers are present naturally around the military camp.

Create these background soldiers from the text description only.

Do not use Riven or Ally Soldier as templates for background soldiers.

Background soldiers must have clearly different faces, hairstyles, body proportions, armor variations, and silhouettes.

Do not duplicate Riven.

Do not duplicate Ally Soldier.

Only ONE Riven exists.

Only ONE Ally Soldier exists.

Only ONE Commander exists.


=== ENVIRONMENT LOCK ===

Use the provided Military Command Camp reference as the strict environment reference.

Preserve the recognizable command tent, rough wooden planning table, military tents, crates, barrels, weapon racks, banners, supplies, worn ground, surrounding pine forest, mountain terrain, and overall environmental design.

The camp is active and occupied by an army preparing for a military operation.

Ordinary allied soldiers move naturally through the background.

Some soldiers carry supplies.

Some check weapons and equipment.

Some prepare tents or organize crates.

Some stand near equipment while preparing for the upcoming operation.

Keep the background activity natural and secondary.

Do not make every soldier stand still and watch the briefing.

The camp should continue functioning around the main characters.

The scene takes place during early evening after sunset.

The last muted warm light remains near the mountain horizon while most of the camp has entered cooler evening shadow.

Small controlled campfires and lanterns provide subtle warm practical light.

The atmosphere is calm, disciplined, and busy.

No battle.

No enemies.

No destruction.


=== TECHNICAL ===

High-end live-action cinematic realistic dark fantasy.

16:9 cinematic widescreen.

Feature-film quality.

Realistic human anatomy.

Natural human movement.

Realistic armor and weapon weight.

Natural facial expressions and body language.

Realistic cloth, hair, firelight, smoke, and environmental physics.

Keep the scene visually clear and grounded.

Avoid excessive cuts.

All character dialogue in this video must be spoken in natural ENGLISH ONLY.

Use clear natural English pronunciation.

Speak the written dialogue exactly as written.

Do not translate the dialogue.

No additional spoken dialogue.

No background conversations.

Natural accurate lip synchronization.

No subtitles.

No captions.

No text.

No watermark.

No logo.


=== GLOBAL ACTION ===

Riven and Ally Soldier are attending a military briefing inside the command camp.

The Commander gives them new orders.

A village is believed to be sheltering enemy forces.

The army has been ordered to move at first light.

Riven does NOT yet know which village the Commander is talking about.

She does NOT recognize the mission as connected to her home.

Ally Soldier also treats this as a normal military assignment.

Do not reveal Riven's village in this scene.

Do not show the village.

Do not suggest visually that Riven already knows the truth.

The discovery happens later.


=== SCENE ===

Begin inside the active Military Command Camp during early evening.

The camp is already functioning around the characters.

Background allied soldiers naturally prepare equipment and supplies.

Riven and Ally Soldier approach the command area together.

The Commander stands beside the rough wooden planning table outside the command tent.

A simple military map and a few practical planning materials rest on the table.

Do not show readable writing or labels on the map.

Riven and Ally Soldier stop in front of the Commander.

They remain standing.

The Commander looks at them.

His manner is calm and professional.

Commander:

"We have new orders."

Riven and Ally Soldier listen.

The Commander briefly looks down toward the military map and indicates a general location with his hand.

Commander:

"A village is sheltering enemy forces."

Riven remains attentive.

She shows no recognition.

No shock.

No fear.

No emotional reaction suggesting that she knows the village.

For Riven, this is still an ordinary military briefing.

The Commander continues.

Commander:

"We move at first light."

Allow a brief natural silence.

Riven looks toward the map.

Ally Soldier also studies the planning table.

Both characters understand the order.

Riven gives a restrained professional nod.

Ally Soldier does the same.

The Commander returns his attention to the planning table and the preparations around him.

The briefing is finished.

Riven and Ally Soldier turn away from the command area.

They begin walking through the camp together.

Do not add dialogue between them.

Around them, ordinary soldiers continue preparing for the operation.

Some carry crates or equipment.

Others check weapons.

The camp remains active.

Riven walks naturally beside Ally Soldier.

She remains calm.

She still has no idea that the village mentioned in the briefing is her home.

As Riven and Ally Soldier move away from the command area, keep the Commander visible briefly behind them beside the planning table.

The military camp continues preparing for first light.

CUT.


=== END STATE FOR CONTINUITY ===

Riven and Ally Soldier have received their new military orders.

They know that a village is believed to be sheltering enemy forces.

They know the army will move at first light.

Riven does NOT know that the target is her home village.

Ally Soldier does NOT know either.

Riven has not questioned the order.

There is no conflict between Riven and the Commander yet.

The army continues preparing for the operation.

The identity of the village remains unrevealed.


=== MOOD ===

Professional.

Controlled.

Military.

Quietly serious.

The scene should initially feel like a normal mission briefing.

Do not make the Commander appear evil.

Do not make Riven suspicious.

Do not create dramatic foreshadowing through exaggerated reactions.

The audience should experience the briefing as ordinary military procedure.

The emotional change comes later when Riven discovers which village the order refers to.
